verdict: Disney earned $1.9B for shareholders as segment profit rose 27% to $3.9B — Experiences profit hit $3.1B and streaming losses narrowed sharply — even though total revenue was flat at $23.5B.

segments.name: Services
segments.note: Streaming subscriptions, TV networks and channels, park tickets and hotel stays — the large majority of Disney's money.

segments.name: Products
segments.note: Merchandise, food and drinks, and other things Disney physically sells.

segmentNote: Segment operating income: Entertainment $874M, Sports -$103M (a loss), Experiences $3,105M (before corporate costs).

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Marketing the movies, shows and parks, and running the company.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: The wear and tear on parks, cruise ships and equipment, spread over their working lives.

otherDetail: Interest expense, net, of $246M on Disney's debt, partly offset by $181M of equity income from companies Disney part-owns.
follow100Note: Of the $9.14 kept as profit per $100 of revenue, $1.02 belongs to noncontrolling partners — Disney shareholders' share was $8.11. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.
footerNote: Of the $2,151M of net income, $240M belongs to noncontrolling interests, leaving $1,911M attributable to Disney (the $1.04 EPS figure). The earnings release reports one combined cost line; the split between cost of services/products, SG&A and depreciation comes from the Q1 FY24 10-Q.

takeaways.title: Segment profit jumped
takeaways.text: Total segment operating income rose 27% to $3,876M: Experiences grew 8% to $3,105M, Entertainment more than doubled to $874M, and Sports narrowed its loss to $103M on the timing of College Football Playoff games.

takeaways.title: Streaming losses shrank fast
takeaways.text: Entertainment direct-to-consumer (Disney+ and Hulu) lost $138M, versus a $984M loss a year ago, as price rises and ad revenue grew. Hulu added 1.2 million subscribers; Disney+ Core lost 1.3 million after a price increase.

takeaways.title: Profit rose even on flat revenue
takeaways.text: Revenue was flat at $23,549M, but cost cuts — over $500M of savings realized in the quarter — lifted EPS 49% to $1.04 and free cash flow swung to $886M from -$2,155M a year ago.

oneTimers: Disney's 'excluding certain items' EPS of $1.22 adds back $451M of amortization of the Fox (TFCF) and Hulu acquisition intangible assets ($0.18 per share) — a non-cash purchase-accounting charge Disney excludes every quarter. There were no restructuring or impairment charges this quarter.
